canvas-01.description: Printed sheet 63, the title sheet of the Avon section of the New Jersey coast volume, at the south-east corner of the borough. The map part covers the blocks between 1st Avenue and Ocean Avenue from just north of Garfield Avenue south to Riverside Avenue and the shore of the Shark River. North is close to the top of the page. The blocks are cut into narrow numbered building lots, almost all of them still vacant in 1905: a single two-and-a-half-storey dwelling stands on Garfield Avenue, and the top edge of the sheet shows the corner of a large hotel drawn in full on sheet 70. Each block is split by a 20 foot alley, numbered 1 to 4 on the sheet. The lots facing Ocean Avenue run east-west and are shallower towards the south. East of Ocean Avenue the sheet shows the dashed line of the Board Walk and the bulkhead line along the beach; the rest of the right half of the page is taken by the title cartouche (Insurance Maps of Avon, New Jersey, Sanborn Map Company, 1905), a legend box, notes on population, water supply and fire department, and a small key map of the whole borough between Sylvan Lake and the Shark River with Bradley Beach and Belmar beyond. Those title and key areas are left out of the georeferenced part. Riverside Avenue curves along the river bank at the bottom of the sheet; a compass rose and scale bar sit in the lower margin.
notes: Canvas labelled 'Overview' in the manifest; it is printed sheet 63, the title sheet with the key map.
The title cartouche says 'Scale 50 ft. to an inch' but the scale bar says 60 ft; the fitted scale (6.63 px/ft) agrees with every other sheet, which are drawn at 60 ft.
Riverside Avenue along the Shark River has no modern street on its line.
Population printed as 500 in winter, 2000 in summer; water from the East Jersey Coast Water Co.

Printed sheet 63 (canvas labelled Overview): title sheet with the map of 1st Av to Ocean Av, Garfield Av to Riverside Av; title cartouche, legend and key map at right left out of the mask. Cartouche says 50 ft, scale bar 60 ft; fit agrees with 60 ft. North near up.

sheet-64-1.description: Printed sheet 64, main part, at the north-west of Avon between Woodland Avenue and Sylvan Lake. The sheet is turned so that north lies to the right: 5th, 4th and 3rd Avenues run across the page and Woodland and Norwood Avenues run down it. It covers the two blocks between Woodland and Norwood Avenues from 5th Avenue to 3rd Avenue, divided by a 20 foot alley, and the wedge of land west of Norwood Avenue where West End Avenue and Lakeside Avenue run diagonally along the head of the lake towards Main Avenue at the top edge. The blocks are cut into narrow numbered lots; there are a few two-storey dwellings along Woodland Avenue between 5th and 4th Avenues and many vacant lots. The head of Sylvan Lake, drawn in blue, runs diagonally across the sheet, with the lake's name lettered along it. The lower right of the page holds an inset of the land between Main Avenue and the railroad, which is a separate part. Top-margin blocks belong to sheet 66.
notes: Main Avenue of 1905 is today's Main Street (NJ 71).
The sheet is turned: north points to the right.

Turned (north to the right). Part 1: Woodland to Norwood Av, 5th to 3rd Av, West End and Lakeside Av along Sylvan Lake. Part 2: inset of Main Av at Norwood Av by the railroad (Consumers Coal & Supply Co.). 60 ft.

sheet-64-2.description: Inset on printed sheet 64 showing the strip of land between Main Avenue and the New York and Long Branch Railroad at the north-west corner of Avon, from Norwood Avenue east to the head of Sylvan Lake. It is drawn at the same scale and orientation as the main part of the sheet (north to the right), inside a heavy frame in the lake area of the page. The inset shows the yard of Consumer's Coal and Supply Co.: a lime kiln, buildings for grain, hay, lime and cement, firewood and cord wood, an ice house, a coal trestle on a siding from the railroad, and a storage building for contractors' machinery with a wind fan nearby. Two small blocks with dwellings face Norwood Avenue at the left. Main Avenue, 100 feet wide, runs across the lower half of the inset with an 8 inch water pipe; the stubs of West End Avenue and Lakeside Avenue leave it towards the lake, and the edge of Sylvan Lake is drawn at the lower right.
notes: Main Avenue of 1905 is today's Main Street (NJ 71).
Placed from one detected junction (Main Street / Norwood Avenue) at the atlas scale and the inset's own measured rotation; Lakeside Avenue / Main Street, also detected, agrees within 3 m.
Railroad lettered New York & Long Branch R.R.; firm lettered Consumer's Coal & Supply Co.

Turned (north to the right). Part 1: Woodland to Norwood Av, 5th to 3rd Av, West End and Lakeside Av along Sylvan Lake. Part 2: inset of Main Av at Norwood Av by the railroad (Consumers Coal & Supply Co.). 60 ft.

sheet-65.description: Printed sheet 65, the south-west corner of Avon on Shark River Bay, between Lincoln Avenue and the Shark River and from the New York and Long Branch Railroad east to 5th Avenue. North is near the top of the page. Main Avenue and Bay Avenue run down the sheet at a slight slant, and the blocks between them and 5th Avenue are cut by Washington and Jefferson Avenues and divided into narrow numbered lots, almost all vacant. A 20 foot alley runs north-south between Main and 5th Avenues. Riverside Avenue runs diagonally along the bank of the Shark River in the lower right. The railroad runs down the left side of the sheet on a causeway past Shark River Bay, which is drawn in blue at the upper left, and crosses the river at the bottom left; a boat house stands on the river bank at the foot of Bay Avenue. Only a few dwellings are drawn, near Main Avenue and Lincoln Avenue. A compass rose and the scale bar are in the lower right.
notes: Main Avenue of 1905 is today's Main Street (NJ 71).
Bay Avenue and Riverside Avenue have no modern street on their line and were not used for control.
5th Avenue / Lincoln Avenue at the top edge was measured from a lot line and is excluded.
SW corner: Lincoln to Shark River, railroad to 5th Av; Main Av (now Main Street), Bay Av, Riverside Av. 60 ft, north near up.

sheet-66.description: Printed sheet 66, the business centre of Avon along Main Avenue and the railroad, from Norwood Avenue south to Lincoln Avenue and from Laird Avenue and West Sylvania east to 5th Avenue. North is near the top of the page. The New York and Long Branch Railroad runs down the sheet west of Main Avenue. Along Main Avenue stand the fire house (one double-cylinder chemical engine, one supply wagon, 600 feet of hose), a Methodist church, Sofield's stables, a blacksmith and woodwork shop, a grain and hay store, a plumber, a confectionery and tobacco shop with an insurance office and barber, ice houses, a court room and jail and a building of tenements. West of the railroad the sheet shows scattered dwellings along Laird Avenue and West Sylvania, which run diagonally at the left edge. The blocks east of Main Avenue towards 5th Avenue are cut into narrow numbered lots, many vacant. A compass rose is drawn in the lower left.
notes: Main Avenue of 1905 is today's Main Street (NJ 71); West Sylvania is today's West Sylvania Avenue (NJ 35).
Business centre on Main Av and the railroad, Norwood to Lincoln Av, Laird Av and W. Sylvania to 5th Av. 60 ft, north near up.

sheet-67.description: Printed sheet 67, the south-central part of Avon between 5th Avenue and 3rd Avenue from Lincoln Avenue south to the Shark River. The sheet is drawn at 60 feet to an inch (printed scale bar) and turned so that north lies towards the right of the page; streets run square to the borough grid. Washington and Lincoln Avenues run down the page; Jefferson Avenue runs diagonally from 5th Avenue to meet Washington Avenue at 4th Avenue, and Riverside Avenue runs diagonally along the bank of the Shark River at the left, where the river is drawn in blue. The blocks are cut into narrow numbered lots, nearly all vacant; a handful of dwellings stand on the block between Washington and Lincoln Avenues near 5th Avenue. A 20 foot alley divides the Washington-Lincoln blocks. A compass rose sits beside the river and the scale bar in the lower left corner.
notes: Riverside Avenue has no modern street on its line.
The sheet is turned: north points to the right.
Turned (north to the right): 5th to 3rd Av, Lincoln Av to Shark River; Jefferson and Riverside Av diagonal. 60 ft.

sheet-68.description: Printed sheet 68, the centre of Avon between 5th Avenue and 3rd Avenue from Lincoln Avenue north to Woodland Avenue. The sheet is drawn at 60 feet to an inch (printed scale bar) and turned so that north lies towards the right of the page; streets run square to the borough grid. Lincoln, Garfield, Sylvania and Woodland Avenues run down the page and 4th Avenue crosses the middle. Each block is split by a 20 foot alley and cut into narrow numbered lots. The 1st Baptist Church (heated by stoves, lit by electricity) and its hall stand at 5th Avenue between Garfield and Sylvania Avenues, beside the Home of the Merciful Saviour for Crippled Children. Dwellings, mostly two to two-and-a-half storeys, are scattered along Garfield and Sylvania Avenues, with more vacant lots towards Lincoln Avenue. A 6 inch water pipe is marked in 5th Avenue and along Garfield Avenue. Blocks in the top and bottom margins belong to sheets 66, 69 and 71.
notes: The sheet is turned: north points to the right.
Turned (north to the right): 5th to 3rd Av, Lincoln to Woodland Av. Pilot sheet. 60 ft.

sheet-69.description: Printed sheet 69, the north-central part of Avon on the south shore of Sylvan Lake, between 3rd Avenue and 1st Avenue from Lakeside Avenue south to Sylvania Avenue. North is near the top of the page. Lakeside Avenue runs along the lake shore, which is drawn in blue across the top of the sheet with the lake's name. Norwood, Woodland and Sylvania Avenues cross the sheet and 2nd Avenue runs down its middle. The blocks are split by 20 foot alleys and cut into narrow numbered lots. Two hotels stand here: The Marlborough on Norwood Avenue at 2nd Avenue and The Buckingham on Sylvania Avenue east of 2nd Avenue; St. John's Church (Protestant Episcopal) is near 1st Avenue south of Norwood Avenue. Dwellings line Woodland and Sylvania Avenues. A compass rose stands at the upper left and the scale bar on Sylvania Avenue at the left.
notes: Hotels lettered The Marlborough and The Buckingham; church lettered St. John's Church (Prot. Episc.).
3rd to 1st Av, Lakeside (Sylvan Lake) to Sylvania Av. 60 ft, north near up.

sheet-70.description: Printed sheet 70, the north-east corner of Avon between 1st Avenue and the ocean, from Sylvan Lake south to below Sylvania Avenue. North is near the top of the page. Lakeside Avenue runs along the lake shore at the top, with a bridge over the lake outlet, and East End, Norwood, Woodland and Sylvania Avenues run east to Ocean Avenue. The U.S. Life Saving Station stands on the block between Lakeside and East End Avenues. Along the beach east of Ocean Avenue are rows of bath houses, a confectionery and a pavilion on the Board Walk; the shoreline of the Atlantic Ocean is drawn down the right edge. At the bottom of the sheet is the Avon Inn with its kitchen, steam laundry, barber and drug store and bowling alleys, with a note on its water tanks supplied by pumps from wells and gravity pressure available only in the summer season. The blocks are split by 20 foot alleys and cut into numbered lots with scattered two-and-a-half-storey dwellings.
notes: Ocean Avenue's 1905 west line differs from today's centreline; its junctions were detected with residuals under 0.5 m.
1st Av to the ocean, Sylvan Lake to below Sylvania Av; Life Saving Station, Avon Inn, bath houses. 60 ft, north near up. Present although the catalog says sheet 70 wanting.

sheet-71.description: Printed sheet 71, the south-east part of Avon between 3rd Avenue and 1st Avenue from Garfield Avenue south to the Shark River. North is near the top of the page. Garfield, Lincoln and Washington Avenues cross the sheet and 2nd Avenue runs down its middle; Riverside Avenue runs diagonally along the bank of the Shark River at the bottom, drawn in blue. The blocks are split by 20 foot alleys and cut into narrow numbered lots. The Oxford hotel stands near 2nd Avenue at the top of the sheet; dwellings are scattered along Garfield and Lincoln Avenues, and the blocks towards Washington Avenue and the river are almost entirely vacant. A compass rose and the scale bar are at the lower left.
notes: Riverside Avenue has no modern street on its line.
Hotel lettered The Oxford.
3rd to 1st Av, Garfield Av to Shark River. 60 ft, north near up.
